# Watch · 值更 (AgentRelay) — Full Context for AI Search & LLMs

> Canonical Site: https://relay.bobochang.cn/ (zh-CN) | https://relay.bobochang.cn/en/ (en)
> Author: can4hou6joeng4 (https://bobochang.cn)
> Generated: 2026-11-18. License: MIT

---

## 1. Core System & Overview

Watch (Chinese: 值更, also called AgentRelay) is a free, local-only CLI and macOS desktop tool that hands an in-progress AI coding-agent session (conversation history, tool call events, and exact working directory) between Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, OpenCode, Kimi CLI, Pi and Grok CLI when an agent hits account usage limits or gets stuck.

### Key Safety Constraints
- 100% Local Execution: Watch has no cloud relay, server, or analytics. It reads and writes local disk stores directly.
- Strict CWD Matching: Prevents code edits across different workspaces or Git worktrees.
- Target Writer Guard: Direct writes to Codex inspect native per-thread writer locks (~/.codex/thread-writer-locks/<id>.lock via lsof) and pre/post content fingerprints.
- OpenCode SQLite Isolation: Multi-table writes (sessions, messages, parts) execute in one SQLite transaction and roll back on failure; supports WATCH_OPENCODE_DB isolation.
- Tool Call Degradation: Complex proprietary tool call events are downgraded to structured text representations in target agents.

---

## 2. Intent-to-Route Decision Matrix

| User Intent / Failure Scenario | Source Agent | Target Agent | Handoff Route | Primary Command | Data Preservation & Safety |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 5-hour / weekly usage limit reached | Claude Code | OpenAI Codex | Official Desktop Import | `npm run watch -- import-codex prepare <id> --cwd /absolute/project --desktop-project --experimental --json` | Target directory/configuration binding and Watch import lock; tool calls degrade to text; review the plan, then run `npm run watch -- import-codex confirm <plan-id> --experimental --json` |
| Context window full | Claude Code | Claude Code | Native `/compact` | `/compact` (in Claude) | Uses the current agent; context capacity depends on model and configuration |
| Switch to local offline model | Claude Code | OpenCode | SQLite Store Adapter | `npm run watch -- open <id> --to opencode` | Single SQLite transaction rollback on failure; custom DB via WATCH_OPENCODE_DB; offline use requires a configured local provider |
| Still limited after using the subscription's own reset | Claude Code | OpenAI Codex | Official Desktop Import | `npm run watch -- import-codex prepare <id> --cwd /absolute/project --desktop-project --experimental --json` | Watch does not inspect or consume quota resets; review the plan before explicit confirmation |
| Resume past session in original agent | Any | Same Agent | Native Resume | `claude --resume <id>` / `codex resume <id>` / `opencode -s <id>` | Native CLI history lookup; no translation required |
| Target CLI has no adapter or its native format changed | Any | Unsupported CLI | Read-only Prompt Handoff | `npm run watch -- prompt <id> --cwd /absolute/project --json` | Produces Markdown only; writes no target files and launches no CLI; trimmed turns and source state are disclosed in the document and findings |

---

## 3. Technical Guides (Full Text & Official Procedures)

### Guide: Continuing in Codex After Claude Code Reaches Usage Limit (Claude Code 达到使用限额后转入 Codex 继续实操指南)
- URL (zh): https://relay.bobochang.cn/guides/claude-code-limit-to-codex/
- URL (en): https://relay.bobochang.cn/en/guides/claude-code-limit-to-codex/
- Direct Answer (en): When Claude Code reports a five-hour or weekly limit, /compact does not restore quota. Watch reads only the local ~/.claude/projects/<encoded-cwd>/<session>.jsonl, checks the working directory, and copies that record into Codex. The original file stays unchanged. Tool events may become text.
- 核心解答 (zh): Claude Code 提示 5 小时或周限额时，/compact 不能恢复额度。Watch 只读取本机 ~/.claude/projects/<编码目录>/<会话>.jsonl，核对工作目录后转入 Codex；原文件不改，工具事件可能降级为文本。

#### Procedure Steps:
1. **Step 1: Verify source session ID and working directory**: Locate the active Claude Code session ID. History is stored under ~/.claude/projects/<encoded-cwd>/<session-id>.jsonl. Ensure the directory path (cwd) matches the actual project workspace to prevent worktree and repository misalignments.
1. **Step 2: Ensure target project exists in Codex Desktop**: This guide uses Watch's --desktop-project route, which requires the project to be registered in Codex Desktop and synchronized with app-server. Open the destination directory in Codex Desktop before preparing the plan. This is a guard for this desktop handoff route.
1. **Step 3: Prepare the import plan (Prepare)**: Select the source session and click OpenAI Codex in Watch Desktop, or run prepare. Watch checks the source, working directory, destination and Codex version, then saves a local import plan. It does not submit the session import or acquire the Watch target lock used during confirmation. The native version check may maintain its own runtime files, so this is not an entirely write-free operation.
1. **Step 4: Confirm import and review degradation items (Confirm)**: Review the previewed message count, working directory, and tool call traces. Explicitly confirm to initiate the transfer via the local Codex app-server import protocol. Note that tool call events may degrade into text representations.
1. **Step 5: Launch the target client independently (Open)**: Once confirmed, open Codex Desktop using the app interface or resume command. Import and opening are strictly separated: if launching fails, retry opening only without repeating the import phase.

#### Frequently Asked Questions:
- **Q: Does Watch bypass or reset Claude Code rate limits?**
  A: No. Watch is a local handoff utility. It does not tamper with Anthropic accounts or inject credits; it transfers locally saved session artifacts into another agent that has active capacity.
- **Q: Can I immediately prompt Codex to continue coding?**
  A: Codex will inspect the imported conversation history, but model performance on resumed tasks depends on the target agent's context capacity. We recommend asking Codex to summarize the current objective before assigning new code edits.
- **Q: What happens if I submit an import twice?**
  A: Watch enforces persistent locks and plan idempotency. Duplicate prepare requests for the same source and directory return the existing plan without duplicating records.

---

### Guide: OpenCode, Claude & Codex Bidirectional Session Handoff Guide (OpenCode 与 Claude/Codex 双向会话接力与 SQLite 数据隔离指南)
- URL (zh): https://relay.bobochang.cn/guides/opencode-handover-sqlite-isolation/
- URL (en): https://relay.bobochang.cn/en/guides/opencode-handover-sqlite-isolation/
- Direct Answer (en): OpenCode keeps sessions in ~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db. WATCH_OPENCODE_DB points Watch at another file. Watch writes sessions, messages, and parts in one SQLite transaction and rolls back if it fails. Unsupported tool fields become text. Later replies depend on the model you configure.
- 核心解答 (zh): OpenCode 的会话在本机 ~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db，可用 WATCH_OPENCODE_DB 换库。Watch 用一次 SQLite 事务写入 sessions、messages、parts；事务失败会回滚。不支持的工具参数降级为文本，续写质量取决于你配置的模型。

#### Procedure Steps:
1. **Step 1: Identify source session ID and working directory**: Locate your active session ID. Claude Code stores files in ~/.claude/projects/; Codex in ~/.codex/sessions/; OpenCode indexes sessions via globally unique IDs. Verify that the working directory is an absolute path to maintain project boundary alignment.
1. **Step 2: Preflight target database status (Check)**: Run --check to preview the destination and pending turns, then inspect writable, blocked and warnings. When pending turns exist, OpenCode preflight checks the storage layout and an existing target's revert state; 2.x layouts are read-only. It does not write the target session, test write permissions or acquire a SQLite write lock, and cannot guarantee that a later write will face no concurrent changes.
1. **Step 3: Execute bidirectional handoff (Handoff)**: Select the source session in Watch Desktop and target OpenCode, or run the CLI open command. Watch extracts incremental turns, executes atomic SQLite transactions across sessions, messages, and parts, and issues the destination session ID.
1. **Step 4: Resume session natively in OpenCode (Resume)**: After conversion, execute opencode -s <session-id> in the workspace directory or trigger the launch button in Watch Desktop. OpenCode loads the recorded conversation in that working directory.

#### Frequently Asked Questions:
- **Q: What is the advantage of OpenCode's SQLite storage over JSONL?**
  A: A SQLite transaction commits a session write as a unit and rolls it back on failure. SQLite does not provide row-level write locks; concurrent writers can still contend for the database. WATCH_OPENCODE_DB redirects Watch's reads and writes to a separate test database; it does not automatically change the database used by the native OpenCode client.
- **Q: Are custom model reasoning thoughts retained when handing off out of OpenCode?**
  A: Watch copies the saved user prompts, assistant text, thinking traces, and tool outputs it can map. Unsupported tool fields become text, so the copy is not a complete replica of the OpenCode row.
- **Q: How does Watch prevent working directory mismatch?**
  A: Watch records the selected absolute cwd and returns a complete resume command that changes directory before running opencode -s <session-id>. Verify the working directory and use that complete command; opencode -s alone does not include Watch's directory change. A cwd record is not a file-access sandbox, so check paths and permissions in the destination tool as well.

---

### Guide: Context Window Full vs Usage Limits in Claude Code: Practical Guide (Claude Code 上下文满与账户限额的本质区别与应对实操指南)
- URL (zh): https://relay.bobochang.cn/guides/context-limit-vs-usage-limit-handoff/
- URL (en): https://relay.bobochang.cn/en/guides/context-limit-vs-usage-limit-handoff/
- Direct Answer (en): A full context window means this conversation is too long: run /compact or /clear inside Claude Code. An account limit names a reset time, and /compact does nothing then. Watch neither enlarges the window nor restores quota. It copies the saved session into another agent that can still run.
- 核心解答 (zh): 上下文满了是这一次对话太长，在 Claude Code 里执行 /compact 或 /clear。账户限额到了会给出重置时间，此时 /compact 无效。Watch 不扩大上下文，也不恢复额度，只把已保存的会话记录转入另一个仍可用的 Agent。

#### Procedure Steps:
1. **Step 1: Check terminal error signals to identify the limit type**: If Claude reports "exceeded your limit" with a reset time, it is an account Usage Limit: running /compact will fail because the model quota is exhausted; wait for reset or hand off to Codex / OpenCode. If Claude reports conversation length limits or high latency, it is a Context Window Limit: run /compact.
1. **Step 2: Apply native resolution for context length (/compact & /clear)**: Inside Claude Code, run /compact to compress conversation history into a distilled summary. If historical investigative turns are no longer required, run /clear to begin a clean slate in the current workspace.
1. **Step 3: Save session state upon hitting account usage quotas**: Verify Claude Code has flushed its session transcript to ~/.claude/projects/<enc-cwd>/<session-id>.jsonl. Use Watch to inspect the working directory and target readiness for Codex or OpenCode.
1. **Step 4: Hand off to an alternative agent without repeating context**: Use Watch to convert the recorded reasoning and test results into the destination agent's format, then resume in the new CLI with full preceding context.

#### Frequently Asked Questions:
- **Q: Will /compact discard code modifications made on disk?**
  A: No. File edits already exist on your local filesystem. /compact only compresses in-memory conversation history. However, detailed sub-error messages may be summarized.
- **Q: Why does /compact fail when hitting an account usage limit?**
  A: /compact organizes conversation history; it does not restore account quota, and a request to generate a summary may also be blocked by the limit. You can wait for the reset, choose another available tool and follow a validated handoff route, or export a shorter document with watch prompt for manual handoff. Watch does not restore or bypass quota.
- **Q: Does handing off to Codex or OpenCode reset context?**
  A: Handoff carries saved history that can be converted into the destination session, where it still consumes context. Watch does not enlarge the window or automatically summarize to a target token budget, so it cannot guarantee that saturation is resolved. To shorten the input, use the destination tool's native compaction or export a shorter handoff document with watch prompt presets and --last, then review its omission disclosures.

---

### Guide: What Claude Opus 5.5 changes about five-hour limits, and what to do when you are still capped (Claude Opus 5.5 提高 5 小时限额之后，限额和会话接力分别怎么处理)
- URL (zh): https://relay.bobochang.cn/guides/opus-5-5-five-hour-limit/
- URL (en): https://relay.bobochang.cn/en/guides/opus-5-5-five-hour-limit/
- Direct Answer (en): Opus 5.5 raises the five-hour limit on Pro, Max, Team, and seat-based Enterprise, and adds one reset you can save. It does not remove the limit. Watch does not read or raise Claude quota. Hand the saved session to Codex only after that official reset is still not enough.
- 核心解答 (zh): Opus 5.5 提高的是 Pro、Max、Team 和按席位 Enterprise 的 5 小时限额，并给一次可保存的重置，不是取消限额。Watch 不读取、不增加 Claude 额度。官方重置用完后若仍被拦住，再把本机会话转入 Codex。

#### Procedure Steps:
1. **Step 1: Read which limit the product is reporting**: A message that you have exceeded the current usage limit, with a reset time, is an account limit. /compact does not restore that quota. A message about conversation length is a context-window limit. Compact inside Claude Code. Switching the model name is not the fix for either case.
1. **Step 2: Use the plan’s own five-hour limit and saved reset**: The higher five-hour limit applies to Pro, Max, Team, and seat-based Enterprise. The savable reset belongs to the Claude subscription. Watch has not verified a CLI flag that stores it, so do not assume a Watch command has banked the reset for you. If you are still blocked after the reset Anthropic provides, then consider another agent.
1. **Step 3: Hand off only if Claude is still blocked**: Watch does not read, raise, or bypass Claude quota. It copies a session already saved on disk into Codex, keeping the working directory. Follow the existing guide, Continuing in Codex after Claude Code reaches its usage limit: check the session id and directory, then prepare, confirm, and open Codex separately.

#### Frequently Asked Questions:
- **Q: Does Claude Opus 5.5 remove the five-hour usage limit?**
  A: No. Anthropic increased the five-hour limit on Pro, Max, Team, and seat-based Enterprise. The limit still exists, and hitting it still shows a reset time.
- **Q: Can Watch spend the savable rate-limit reset for me?**
  A: No. That control belongs to the Claude subscription. Watch does not sign in to a Claude account, and it neither stores nor spends the reset.
- **Q: Do I still hand the session to Codex after the limit increase?**
  A: Only when the official reset is not enough and Codex still has quota. The handoff steps did not change with Opus 5.5.

---

### Guide: Why resume Opens an Empty Session: Detecting and Recovering 0-Turn Sessions (为什么 resume 打开是空会话：0 轮会话的识别与恢复)
- URL (zh): https://relay.bobochang.cn/guides/empty-session-resume-check/
- URL (en): https://relay.bobochang.cn/en/guides/empty-session-resume-check/
- Direct Answer (en): An empty session after resume usually means the file has no turns left: a legitimate empty session created by watch new, content cleared with only a placeholder header left, or a zero-byte file. Check the turn count on the chain-tip row in watch status. Watch does not rebuild history for you; restore the file from backup, rebind to another session, or start a new chain.
- 核心解答 (zh): resume 打开空会话，通常是因为这条会话文件里没有可继续的对话：可能是 watch new 建出的合法空会话、内容被清空只剩占位头，也可能是 0 字节文件。用 watch status 看链尾行的轮数即可判断；Watch 不会替你重建历史，只能从备份恢复、换绑到另一条会话，或另起一条链。

#### Procedure Steps:
1. **Step 1: Read the chain-tip row in status**: Run watch status. Since v0.1.90 the chain-tip row shows its turn count, for example a chain tip with 12 turns; a 0-turn parse says it parsed 0 turns and points at the warning above; an unreadable or missing file carries no count. In JSON the fields are chainTipTurns and chainTipEmpty, and chainTipTurns exists only when the parse succeeds. With several chains, the tip row in watch chain list carries the same count (v0.1.93); when in doubt, store.emptyTips in watch doctor lists tips that parse to 0 turns (v0.1.92). watch new --json also reports the actual parsed turn count (v0.1.94): claude and pi write a placeholder user message, so it shows 1 turn, while codex, grok and opencode show 0. Since v0.1.95, watch usage separates a 0-turn empty session from a session that has content but no recorded usage, so a freshly created chain is no longer reported as a statistics gap. Since v0.1.96, unparsable content lines and Codex compaction records are no longer misreported as empty sessions. Since v0.1.97, a deleted content file is disclosed even when sidecar usage is still available. Since v0.1.98, bad content lines are disclosed in warnings and fields instead of staying silent; since v0.1.99, a bad content line with existing turns is no longer described as a 0-turn parse; since v0.1.100, the text summary separates 0-turn sessions from sessions with usage, and a failed scan says the bad-line count is unknown; since v0.1.101, the 0-turn summary no longer adds a usage-counted clause, and the v0.1.98 note describes a disclosure gap rather than lost usage.
1. **Step 2: Read the four warning cases**: The same result separates zero bytes (the session file is empty), readable 0 turns (parsed 0 turns, nothing to continue), unreadable content (permissions or content), and a missing file (deleted or moved). Each case has a different next step; do not rebind just because you saw the word empty.
1. **Step 3: Check whether it is a brand-new empty session**: A session created by watch new is empty by design. It is the normal starting point for a first chain: the next switch or open --to uses it as the target and merges the source content in. If the chain tip is that new session and you have not switched yet, 0 turns is expected, not damage.
1. **Step 4: Recover according to the case**: Content cleared: restore the file from backup and retry resume; Watch does not rebuild history. Wrong session: rebind the chain tip with watch adopt <provider> --session <another-session-id>. Keep both sides: start another chain with watch chain new <new-chain-name> and leave the original records untouched. Zero bytes with no backup: nothing is left to recover, treat it as a new session.

#### Frequently Asked Questions:
- **Q: Did Watch lose the history when resume opened an empty session?**
  A: Usually not. Watch reads the source first and appends to the target with write guards and atomic writes; a 0-turn session is usually empty from the start (a new session from watch new) or was cleared or truncated earlier. To check whether a Watch write caused it, compare the turn count and warnings in the handoff result with your backup file.
- **Q: What is the difference between 0 turns and 0 bytes?**
  A: 0 turns means the file is readable and has a valid session header but no conversation; it may be a new session or only a placeholder header left behind. 0 bytes means the file itself is empty, from a killed process, a full disk or a half write, and even the session metadata may be gone. The first may just not have started; the second should send you to backups first.
- **Q: Can Watch restore a cleared session automatically?**
  A: No. Watch only reads and writes local session files. It has no history backup and does not invent conversation. Recovery comes from your own backup (Time Machine, copies outside the repo, editor history), and you resume after restoring the file.
- **Q: Does Claude Code delete old sessions on its own?**
  A: Yes. cleanupPeriodDays in the official settings reference defaults to 30 days; after a session starts, Claude Code sweeps transcripts older than that in the background, and expired sessions stop appearing in /resume. The key is allowed in any settings file, so project settings can override user settings. watch doctor reads your user settings, the current directory project settings and the repository-root local settings without writing, but --settings and managed settings are out of scope, so the report is not the effective value. Raising the value only reduces future deletions; it cannot bring back files already removed.

---

### Guide: Using watch prompt When There Is No Adapter (没有适配器时，用 watch prompt 交接会话)
- URL (zh): https://relay.bobochang.cn/guides/prompt-handoff-without-adapter/
- URL (en): https://relay.bobochang.cn/en/guides/prompt-handoff-without-adapter/
- Direct Answer (en): When the target tool has no adapter or its native format just changed, run watch prompt <session-id> to build a read-only Markdown handoff. It writes no session files and starts no CLI; trimming counts and degradations go into the document and the --json findings, and the target must treat it as a summary, not a native session.
- 核心解答 (zh): 目标工具没有适配器或原生格式刚变化时，用 watch prompt <session-id> 生成只读 Markdown 交接文档；它不写会话文件、不启动 CLI，裁剪计数与降级说明写进正文和 --json 的 findings，目标端只能把它当作摘要而不是原生会话。

#### Procedure Steps:
1. **Step 1: Identify the source session and directory**: Pass the session ID explicitly, or pass --cwd and omit the ID. Without an ID, Watch picks the newest readable session in the current directory and marks it as auto-picked in the header; when unsure, name the ID so another session is not mistaken for the source.
1. **Step 2: Choose a profile and window**: --profile minimal|standard|verbose|full controls how much text and how many tool events are expanded. --last N keeps only the newest N user turns and drops the original task description, which the document states. --since-compact starts at the latest compaction summary; when no usable summary exists it does not trim and says so.
1. **Step 3: Review findings and source state**: With --json the result includes markdown, findings and warnings. degraded means the downgrade was disclosed, skipped means content was omitted by your options. The source state, bad lines, usage and branch lines in the document tell you whether it is safe to hand over. A normal repository root also returns a structured sourceBranch ({ branch, repoRoot }; a detached HEAD returns { detached: true, repoRoot }), so scripts do not parse the document.
1. **Step 4: State that it is a summary handoff**: Paste the Markdown or save it as a file and tell the target assistant in the first turn that this is a summary handoff, not a native session. The target cannot resume natively, and tool calls, reasoning and attachments may have been trimmed; anything omitted cannot be recovered from the document.

#### Frequently Asked Questions:
- **Q: Does watch prompt write into the target tool session?**
  A: No. It only reads the source record and prints Markdown; it writes no target session file, opens no database and launches no CLI. When you need native resume in the target, use the launcher or chained path for that adapter; the only official import path is Claude Code to Codex desktop.
- **Q: Why does the document say the first task description was not kept?**
  A: With --last N, Watch starts at the Nth user turn from the end, so earlier turns, including the original task description, are omitted. Drop --last for full background, or use --since-compact with a larger profile; the body lists each trim that actually happened.
- **Q: Can the target assistant continue exactly like a native session?**
  A: No. It receives a summary document without native resume and cannot see trimmed tool execution detail. Ask it in the first turn to restate the task goal and current branch, and only then assign edits.
